Conservative Coding Pt 1 : Maze Generation

0) Summery:

Here is a guide for making a maze generation script to generate, well, maze’s on the fly. Do you want a procedural dungeon, that’s a maze. Do you want procedural cities, that’s a type of maze. Sewer level, maze! It’s, cough, amazing how many applications can be addressed with these principles. We will draw from several generic algorithms that have been around for a long time and adopt them to the Unity platform using c#. Though I am no where near a good coder, these are the general principles that I have experimented with and have found to be useful, along with the MANY many times I have failed in these regards and thus the pitfalls that I have found.

1) The Basic Architecture:

This Image details how I have a current project which utilizes many of the concepts we will be covering. We will be looking at the LevelGen object specifically. It is an (semi) empty object, floating in space (doesn’t matter where) acting as a container for the Maze Generation scripts. Its children, all empty objects, act as containers for objects that are spawned in at run time. These would be the tiles (floors), RoomNodes (objects holding information about the room in question), Walls and so on. Pardon the poor spelling, it is not, uh, my strong point and unity fails to provide spell checking.

I have these broken up these categories as objects as I find it easier if I have to, say, find a specific tile, node, object in those categories. I can simply reference the corresponding child object of the LevelGen object and then look at each “spawned in” child to find what I want to modify or destroy.

Example: I need to remove all “Red” Enemy objects from the level because reasons. If everything was all lumped together, I would be wasting time going though wall objects and tile objects and room nodes and so on. With this setup, I can point to the MobHolder object, loop though that and check each object if it has the quality “Red”, and then destroy it.

2) Game Space Limits:

Let’s create a new C# script and call it MapGen or whatever makes sense to you. I have had issues in the past naming scripts after its container object (LevelGen OBJ contains LevelGen Script), not that Unity has a problem with it, but it can get confusing if you are grabbing the object or the script as a reference. Making this clear is always important. Remember, you write code so that humans can understand it, not the other way around. A machine is perfectly fine with 1’s and 0’s, but us bipeds need something with a bit more bit to it. Hence a reason to comment on your code (which I do very poorly)!

We have 3 important variables to set up. We first need a 2 dimensional array and we will call it Map, like this: 

int [,] Map;

Then we will need to define the MaxX and MaxY size as so: 

public int MaxX; public int MaxY;

This will allow us to define the map size on game start or level load. The “public” declaration allows us to adjust the values in the inspector or from external scripts. Simply click on your MapGen object and look at your script attached to it, if you don’t see your script, make sure you dragged it onto that object. If it compiles, you ought to see two values of MaxX and MaxY sitting there patiently waiting for a value. Remember, you have to now adjust this value in the inspector to have a new value. Public int MaxX = 50; will not adjust this value, though it can be its starting value. This can cause a lot of confusion for those that are not wary of it. Simply stated, if it’s “public” then you MUST modify that value outside the script, either by inspector or by script.

We tie this together with a simple Inish function that will be called on start. As seen in this image for clarity. You may also note that I have included a simple If→Then statement to check if either MaxX or MaxY is less then or equals 0, and to return so as to safe guard our work. When you hand over the control to the computer in these regards, such checks are great, combined with a

Debug.Log(“ something broke at XYZ”);

statement, they can save a ton of bug hunting time. Insert obligatory aliens 2 reference here. Debug.Log(“XYZ”); is your greatest friend making something and worst enemy for a finished product.

Answering Questions About Nuclear Power | NeuroLogica Blog

Slightly interesting but I wouldn't have posted it.

The best point is seldom, if ever, do you hear the word baseload in public. It is the single most critical point and is why solar and wind will never be more than a rolling blackout on the face of your nation. They are an unusably bad idea.

It is also necessary to leave aside all the hand waving about whether or not Carbon Dioxide has any effect at all on global temperatures. Fanatics opposed to nuclear power have demonstrated (as fanatics are so prone to doing) that facts are not a compelling argument for them. Most people that are not fanatics opposed to nuclear power knew or at least have come to see, that not a single one of the predictions of catastrophic global warming have come true. In the last 3 decades or so the empirical observation that everything they said was hopelessly wrong is getting hard to cover up.

A down side for nuclear is he skips over some very serious concerns about life extension programs. Granted Germany and Japan turned off FULLY functional reactors for no good reason on earth. But in general most reactors are closer to 70 years old than 30. These things do wear out. It is overly simplistic to ignore that.

But my biggest complaint is talking about nuclear "waste". IF spent fuel really was a permanent (in human life terms) problem this would be a valid reason to not use it. His idea to burry it in Yucca Mountain is as stupid as the people that dug the hole in the first place. What he SHOULD have said in the vein of "lack of political will" is the Fast Breeder Reactor.

Almost since the day of its inception we have known that nuclear waste can be reconstituted. It is a painfully simple and FULLY understood process we could loosely call "Reversing radioactive decay". One puts in spent fuel, one gets out weapons grade plutonium. It is the weapons grade part that has all the politicos cowering under their beds. We could of course use the plutonium or mix it with uranium to create MOX. MOX happens to be what we did with the thousands and thousands of pounds of plutonium we got from Russia. Their nuclear weapons were recycled into our power plants.

This is actually about as close as man will ever get to perpetual motion.

The value of recycled fuel would of course go down as the availablity goes up. But for right now as the ultimate irony there is probably 100 trillion dollars worth of fuel that could give us near "free" energy for 100 years.

Until fusion power can be harnessed nuclear fission is not just the best, safest, cheapest alternative -- it is the only one that makes any sense at all!
